_note: THE PICTURES of the search pages, read by pages/make_pictures.py. Each line cuts one still of the museum's film (from the folder MOA_FILM_STILLS names: the stills stay outside the repository) into the sizes a page serves, AVIF and WebP, in pages/pics/img/. A name starts with the wing it belongs to, because the pages' pictures and the site's own share one folder once they are joined, and a name must not be taken twice. 'crop' is a key of 'crops' or a cut of its own as WxH+X+Y; without it the whole frame is taken. The posters (2112x1016, a machine alone on its floor) all take one cut, 1500x844 from the middle: 16:9 like every other plate, so the set reads as one catalogue and the machine stands larger. A name ending in -narrow is a closer cut of the same render at its one scale, which a page gives narrow screens (pics.<name>.narrow). 'share' are the pictures a page shows when its address is shared, 1200x630 as JPEG; a share's 'credit' is a credit its picture owes (map data), which make_pictures.py sets in its bottom right corner. 'plates' are the reproductions the wing hangs, each by its record in the museum's asset store (record, file under the store, sha256, tier, source, licence_url, it108): make_pictures.py cuts each from the store's file only when the store's record still says the same, and the pages' build checks each plate's source line against its record. 'shape' sets the slot a plate fills. A plate with 'still' is shown only through the film's still of the wall that hangs it, cut by the site's own tool under the plate's name: it has no widths here, make_pictures.py checks its record and cuts nothing, and the page's label opens by saying it is a still. A plate's 'crop' (WxH+X+Y on the store's file) cuts it to the painting before its sizes are made. 'line' names the page's label that the plate's source line carries word for word (a cropped plate names the one that says so), 'tier_line' the page's label that stands for the second tier's 'not the painting' sentence (a drawing), 'read_as' how the page reads a record that carries no tier (its tier, the licence the line links, and why), and 'wing_line' the key of the wing page's own label whose line a plate the wing's page already shows carries word for word (the page names it in src_from). 'holder' is the holder's own record of a plate whose file came from elsewhere (its source): the source line links the holder, and make_pictures.py still checks the source against the store. A plate with 'sitemap' false is shown on its page and never listed in the image sitemap (_src/build.py).

read_as.why: the record carries no tier, and its licence is the holder's own CC0 release (National Gallery of Art, Washington, open access): open at its source, the policy's first tier, so the line carries that licence and links it
